utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, I wish to introduce, if I may, Federico Barillas who has been assisting my team for the last four months.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Welcome, Mr. Barillas. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, please continue examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In part 2, section 3 of your report, you referred to the establishment of the VRS, its mission and command structure. And I would like to have the Exhibit 65 ter 05314 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for your orientation, this document is mentioned in the footnotes 21, 199, 200, 201, 238, and 240 in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is a decision of 15 June 1992 related to the command and control of the Army of the Serbia Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, signed by Mr. Karadzic as president of the Presidency. And can we please have the next page in -- in B/C/S and the third page in the English. Yes. Looking at point 4 of this decision, Mr. Theunens, what does the decision show in relation to command and control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision shows in this paragraph, 4, that the operative groups, whereby paragraph 3 explains the operative groups, i.e., the corps, it states that command and control will be performed by the Main Staff, by the Main Staff of the Army of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina will be subordinate -- directly subordinated to the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And the various corps that are mentioned in that decision, were they, indeed, established and was this decision implemented?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, with one addition, that is, that the document does not mention the Drina Corps. The Drina Corps was only established later in the course of November 1992. But the other corps were indeed established and that is, indeed, visible throughout the documents I have included in my report, and the same of course applies to the command and control procedure that is stipulated in paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I request the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3035, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now ask that 65 ter 05284 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, Mr. Karadzic in his capacity as president of the Presidency on the 30th of November, 1992, signs a decision to establish the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, this -- this document is mentioned in the footnote 204 and 205 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the establishment of the Supreme Command, how does this relate to the command and control over the VRS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the document states, Your Honour, the Supreme Command is the highest command-and-control organ over the VRS. It is the Supreme Command - and that we also see through other documents - that issues political directives and related instructions to the Main Staff and the Main Staff then -- which is then implemented throughout the chain of command transform these directives and instructions into further instructions, orders, and commands for the military units.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3036, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in part 2, section 4.6 of your report you provide details on Mr. Karadzic as a supreme commander of the VRS, and you cite quite a number of orders and other documents. I would like to address just a few of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 07186 be brought up on the screen. And, Your Honours, for your orientation, it's footnote 1072 and 1073 in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is an order by General Mladic of the 20th November 1992 related to the holding of the military seminar. Mr. Theunens, does this document reflect on the authority of Mr. Karadzic over the VRS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, Your Honours. As we can see from the introductory paragraph above order where it states: "Pursuant to the request by the Supreme Command ..." and then it identifies Dr. Radovan Karadzic as president of the Presidency and the supreme commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to the attendees in this seminar, any comments on your side who is actually taking part in this seminar?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's -- the seminar is announced or identified as a political and military seminar. And among the attendees we see in paragraph 2 the highest political and military authorities, i.e., president of the Presidency, Mr. Karadzic; a number of governments -- a number of members of the Government of Republika Srpska; representatives of the Main Staff; the core corps command, which refers to the core of the Drina Corps command; and then also subordinate military commanders of the Drina Corps and local civilian authorities, i.e., presidents of municipalities from the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Those military seminars, are they common in the -- in the military and why are they held?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as you will see in my report, I have included this document also in a section which I called "situational awareness." I defined situational awareness in my report as knowledge of the status, intentions, and capabilities of the armed force, i.e., the VRS. Such seminars are intended for at least two reasons, first of all, to allow the political leadership and the military leadership to familiarise themselves with the situation in the corps, including the problems the corps may have or any subordinate unit may have, strong points, and so on. This familiarisation is essential for decision-making. I mean, you need information in order to prepare and plan decisions. In addition, such seminars also allow the political and military leadership to show an interest in activities of subordinate units, i.e., it works as a morale booster for the subordinate units and subordinate commands. I think that for my report I am only -- I only included one document referring to such a seminar, but there are several documents concerning visits by Mr. Karadzic or other senior officials to subordinate military units. So it doesn't necessarily have to be a seminar. The same exchange of information as well as expression of interest in the activities of subordinate units can also be expressed through visits or other exchanges of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3037, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have item P01388 on the screen. And, Your Honour, this document is mentioned in footnote 894 in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is a transcript of the 39th RS Assembly Session of the 24th/25th of March 1994. Mr. Theunens, are you familiar with this particular Assembly session?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I have reviewed it and then included relevant parts in my -- in part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 84 in the English and 68 in the B/C/S just very briefly so that we can see that Mr. Karadzic is speaking, as it says here on -- at the bottom. And can we then have the next page in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And Mr. Karadzic is speaking here and I just quote a few things to you. "I report to you and to the people. Commanders report to me. The commander of the General Staff, commander of corps and brigades. I established a Supreme Command so that I do not make decisions by myself; I did not establish it to use it as a cover. I am the one who signs and decides, and I will be responsible for each decision." And a bit further down, he says: "We should get an analysis for the Supreme Command ..." and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. It's actually -- yeah, it's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It was on the previous --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Last -- last line I think you --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, the last I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I thought you would continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I just wanted to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what does this paragraph reflect in relation to Mr. Karadzic's authority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in this paragraph Mr. Karadzic confirms his authority, his de jure authority as supreme commander of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And did you see this confirmed in other documentation as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, as you will see in the report, on the one hand there is the legislation, there are various decisions by Mr. Karadzic, and on the other hand there are also the various combat documents, including command documents where Mr. Karadzic, as supreme commander, issues -- I mean, he assigns directives, he issues orders and related instructions. And also he's identified by the members of the Main Staff as well as subordinate commanders as the supreme commander in documents, for example, reports they sent to the Main Staff or to Mr. Karadzic throughout the existence of the VRS. I mean by this ending for my report in November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In your report, part 2, you also -- under "supreme commander" you also refer to the ability of Mr. Karadzic to order investigations. And I would like to have in this context one document pulled up, and that's 65 ter 21231. And as it is coming up, it is a decision by Mr. Karadzic to establish an investigative commission from October 1993. From the documentation you reviewed, Mr. Theunens, what event is here to be investigated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this decision by Mr. Karadzic on the 8th of October, 1993, refers to events in Banja Luka between 10 and 17 September 1993, which consisted of a rebellion or sometimes identified as a mutiny of junior military personnel of the 1st Krajina Corps. I have discussed that mutiny in my report. I mean, the people complain about lack of means, lack of compensation for relatives of injured soldiers, corruption, and -- among politicians, and so on. And through this decision Mr. Karadzic orders to investigate these events. Mr. Karadzic issues also other instructions in relation to these events, and those can be found in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at the names of the participants as far as you know them, what kind of authorities are involved in this commission?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the commission includes a number of senior members of the VRS Main Staff. You see, for example, at the end, General Gvero, who is the assistant commander for moral guidance, religious, and legal affairs. We also see senior officials of the Ministry of the Interior. Mr. Bogdan Subotic, for example, was in May 1992 appointed as minister of defence. He was a former JNA general. So it's the most senior political and military officials.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3038, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 05318 be brought up. And, Your Honour, this document is referred to in paragraph -- in footnotes 368, 369, 618, and 787, and 930 in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, looking at the first page, what are we looking at here? What kind of a document is it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document, as it states, is a directive. In part 1 of the report I explain how SFRY armed force doctrine identifies a hierarchy of command documents whereby directives are the highest level. Directives are issued by the Supreme Command and they include instructions for the longer term pertaining to the planning, preparation, and organisation of combat activities. They are more general, but again the emphasis is on the fact that they come from the highest level, and they refer to operations in the mid-long term.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And is -- who signs this particular one, do you need to see the last page?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we see the last page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The -- as we can see on the last page. The document is -- I have the B/C/S in front of me. The document is signed by the supreme commander, Dr. Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 3 in the B/C/S and page 6 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what we find here are war goals listed under number 1 and then there are certain letters. Looking at the war goals listed here, would they relate in any way to the six strategic goals that you describe in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and I have explained that also in my report. The consistency between or the coherence between the six strategic goals and then the directives -- I mean, there are nine directives issued between May 1992 and September 1995. The consistency between the goals as they are defined in the six strategic goals and then the goals for operations, combat operations, as they are identified in these nine directives, which is in itself logical as it reflects the implementation of the principle of unity in command and control, one of the three principles of command and control that applied to SFRY armed forces and subsequently also to the VRS. And we -- if you want I can read them out.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I don't see a need for this. We can read that for ourselves and we also have your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have page 15 in the English and the last page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, it refers here to the command post, including the one for the supreme commander in Pale. And a bit further down there is letter (a) "Regular reporting" mentioned here, even a time is given. According to the military practice would that reporting be done through the chain of command up to the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and that would be done in accordance with the specific instructions that are issued through the order. And the fact that subordinates have to report to their superior on the execution of the tasks they have received from their superior comes from the first principle of command and control, that is, single authority. That there is only one commander who issues orders at the time and it is only to one commander that the subordinates then report on the execution of the order. And obviously -- sorry. And obviously, as I mentioned earlier with the visits and the seminars, the information that is included in the reports of the subordinate unit allows the superior commander to prepare his or -- I mean, his next decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And would this -- what we see here regarding the reporting, would that mean that the supreme commander gets daily reports?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot -- sorry, it cannot be derived directly from this document, but as I include an entire section in my report showing that the supreme commander, indeed Mr. Karadzic, receives daily combat reports from the VRS Main Staff throughout the relevant time-period.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be exhibited as P3039.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have Exhibit P00838 brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what we -- as it is coming up, it's General Milovanovic forwarding a directive to the command of the 1st Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we have the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, can you explain what we are looking at here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a similar document as P3039, with the difference that we are talking now about directive number 7, whereas the previous one was directive number 6. But it's the same type of document, it is just a subsequent document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in -- can we please have page 10 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S. Mr. Theunens, on the bottom -- at the bottom it's -- refers to the Drina Corps and the tasking and it says here: "By planned and well thought-out combat operations, create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." From a military point of view, what is the Drina Corps to achieve here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, looking at the context of the events at the time in Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Drina Corps is to eliminate -- I mean, eliminate the Bosnian -- Bosniak, sorry, eliminate the Bosniak, or Muslim, control over the three enclaves. And that is consistent with the strategic objective number 3, i.e., create a corridor in the Drina and eliminate the Drina as a boundary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is already an exhibit. Nothing more to do. I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 02070 be brought up on the screen. And, Your Honour, it is mentioned in footnotes 639 to 641 and 649 of Mr. Theunens' second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, what are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 02070 is an order, as it states in the title, for defence and active combat operations by the command of the Drina Corps. And it actually is the Drina Corps' -- what consists of the Drina Corps' instructions to its subordinate units based on the previous document we saw, i.e., the directive for further operations number 7. Which means that the directive, as it was signed by Mr. Karadzic, includes tasks for the -- for all the VRS main -- units, i.e., the corps. Now, one of these corps, in this case the Drina Corps, is going to use the instructions that are specified in the directive by Mr. Karadzic to issue its own orders to its subordinate units, which is entirely logical with military doctrine in both -- I mean, the SFRY armed forces as well as in other militaries. And when you compare the contents of the two documents, especially when you look at the mission for the Drina Corps, as it is identified in the directive by Mr. Karadzic as well as in the order of the Drina Corps, you will see that they are identical. But the Drina Corps order will then include specific tasks or instructions for its subordinate units, i.e., the brigades and other units included in the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There's no need now to go into this detail. We can read the report ourself and it's also further explained in your report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I request the admittance of this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3040, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would ask that Exhibit 65 ter 13779 be brought up on the screen. And, Your Honours, it is mentioned in the footnotes 891 and -- to 893 in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is an order signed by the deputy commander of the Main Staff, General Milovanovic, to the corps commands. Mr. Theunens, does this order relate to the strategic goals and the overall directives that you explained already to us today and in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honours. I mean, I can give you context if you want, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, this order comes at a time of the events around Gorazde in March/April 1994, when there is pressure of the VRS on the safe -- on the enclave or the safe area. And the international community gets increasingly concerned through UNPROFOR as well as through other mediation efforts and tries to convince the Bosnian Serb -- Bosnian Serbs to stop the pressure or to halt the offensive operations against the enclave, which was also defined as a safe area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have the last page in the English and page 6 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Looking at letter (G) at the bottom of the English, can you please explain to us what it means and what it tells us.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this paragraph, Your Honours, General Milovanovic re-affirms the authority of the supreme commander as well as of the Main Staff or the role of the Main Staff, that is, that they are the only ones who can issue orders to the corps and the brigades. And he also emphasises that units, I mean, the subordinate commanders have to report that they have received the orders, and obviously also that they are implementing them. Now, one could speculate that this means that the fact that this paragraph has to be included in such an explicit way, that it could suggest that there has been a violation or there have been violations of the principle of single authority. I haven't been able to locate -- to identify any specific material for this time-period. I have, however, included a document which is dated, I think, September 1992, when we are talking about the implementation of the order to establish the VRS, which also implies the integration of the TO, Territorial Defence, of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina into the VRS. And there General Mladic reported in some parts of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina there is interference of local authorities who try to maintain control over these TO units instead of integrating them in the VRS. But this dates from -- yeah, the time-period between May and September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The second paragraph of this, (G), tells that there might have been such instances still at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, but as I tried to explain, I conducted searches to do so. It could be that it's related to the issue of Gorazde, where there have -- there was some delay, apparently, in the VRS's implementation of commitments Mr. Karadzic had made to representatives of the international community. But the material I had available to me, I mean the documents I had available to me, did not allow me to draw such a conclusion as to what were the reasons for this apparent delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be admitted as Exhibit P3041.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would now like to have 65 ter 7161 on the screen, and this document is mentioned in footnotes 989, 1020, and 1060. And is a VRS Main Staff document from the 11th of April, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is an example of what I mentioned earlier, i.e., a regular combat report or, as we would call it, situation report that provides an overview of the enemy situation, the situation in the VRS corps, as well as other relevant aspects, following -- or in accordance with the specific template that is always applied for these kind of reports. And this information is then sent to, as we can see on the first page, the president of the Republika Srpska; the chief of the Main Staff of the VJ; the commands of the VRS corps, because they have a need to know this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have the last page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, could you comment on the last paragraph starting with: "Following the decision of the Supreme Command ..." and so on and so forth. Could you comment on this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document -- the regular combat report is dated the 11th of April, 1994, so we are still in the -- what I would call the Gorazde crisis or at least the events related to the Bosnian Serb or VRS offensive operations against the Gorazde enclave or safe area. At one moment in time the international community, i.e., the UN, decides or -- excuse me, UNPROFOR, UNPROFOR decides to call for close air support, which was provided by NATO, in order to prevent the VRS from further progressing. And in response or, as some would say, in retaliation to the use of close air support, the Supreme Command of the VRS, i.e., presided by the supreme commander, Mr. Karadzic, decides to suspend all relations between the Main Staff of the VRS and UN, including also imposing restriction of movements against not only UNPROFOR but also humanitarian organisations. Now, this is one example where such measures are taken. In my report when I discuss the control Mr. Karadzic had over organisations and/or procedures that decided about the passage of humanitarian aid and related convoys through the territory held by the Bosnian Serbs, I provide other examples where at certain occasions the Bosnian Serbs under the command or under the leadership of Mr. Karadzic would decide to stop the free flow or the free passage of such convoys.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender -- I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3042, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit 65 ter 07202 on the screen. And, Your Honour, for your orientation it is mentioned in footnote 1060 in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can you explain what we are looking at here and whether it reflects on the accused's authority at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]

In the second paragraph, according to General Tolimir, Mr. Karadzic expresses his satisfaction with the results that have so far been achieved. And in the third paragraph, Mr. Karadzic issues specific orders to follow-up combat operations and also to provide full protection to UNPROFOR members and the Muslim civilian population, including guaranteeing their safety -- their safety in case of what is described as cross-over to the territory of the Republika Srpska. And this continues in the last paragraph, with additional instructions by Mr. Karadzic in relation to the security and safety of UNPROFOR personnel and Muslim civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Following the -- this order on the full protection of UNPROFOR and civilian Muslim population, according to military doctrine what would the supreme commander and this subordinate Main Staff, what would they have to do after that order has been issued?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously, based on the principle of obligation to implement decisions of superiors, the subordinate commanders have to implement that order. Now, on the basis of the principle of single authority, the subordinate commander has to inform the superior commander of the implementation of the order. Based on the -- on the functions of command and control - and all this is explained in paragraph 1 of the report - one of the functions of command and control is inspection, sometimes translated as control, but control there doesn't mean the same as command and control. But inspection means that the superior who issues the order has to verify the degree of implementation in order to compare the desired result, i.e., what did he want to achieve through his order, with the actual result, i.e., what have the subordinates done. And then, if necessary, to take additional action. And this can go very far, he can issue additional orders, maybe he has to take disciplinary or even judicial measures and so on. But it is obviously -- it's not sufficient to issue an order; as a superior, you also have to verify implementation of the order. Because if you fail to do so, you may be ill-informed about the actual status of not only your own troops but also the progress of operations you have ordered, but it could also undermine your authority because there may be subordinates who for one or the other reason refuse or don't feel like implementing an order. If you don't take measures then, well, it will undermine the authority of the superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in your search and review of materials from that time-period, did you find any documentation that shows that Mr. Karadzic did indeed verify and follow-up whether his order was implemented and applied?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

And then indeed the president, according to this document, has given his agreement with the continuation of operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

If the superior agrees to do something, well, actually he orders it or it becomes an order. And in the third paragraph that is, explicitly, yes, an order but the end result is the same and the value of the instruction is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 5 in the English and page 2 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Kukanjac mentions two things. He states that, generally speaking, the SDS leadership and the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina have, as he calls it, embraced the JNA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, is it not the next page, page 7 in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And he explains -- so why he considers it normal that this kind of good relations have developed between SDS leadership, the Serbian people on the one hand and the JNA 2nd Military District on the other hand. However, he also mentions that there have been a few cases or there have been instances and acts of some criticism on the JNA. He refers to Chetnik tendencies, criticism of some commanding officers. And in relation to this latter aspect, he refers to meetings he will have with what he considers or what he describes as the top leadership of the Serbian people, and he then provides the names of these people, it includes Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see such relationship reflected in other documents that you reviewed, the good relations between the SDS leadership and the JNA?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]

But in addition, there are also several documents referring to specific situations, for example, the establishment of Bosnian Serb TO in various parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina in spring 1992, relationships with SDS Crisis Staffs as well as the take-over operations of municipalities in Northern Bosnia-Herzegovina in spring 1992. And there the specific documents are included in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did. utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And a little bit further down here on that same page we have here the sum -- reflection of some experiences that are addressed, and we find in particular here reference to approaches of certain SDS leaders to the JNA and the Serbian MOD and to attempts of certain SAO authorities bringing army formations under local commands.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would just like to correct what I said in line 9. The transcript states D00235 and it should be D00325. And this happens during summer, fall, and winter 1991. The most important goal of these efforts is to ensure that volunteers are under the command of the JNA, otherwise they have to leave. And Kukanjac is exactly referring to that, that according to his experiences there are situations where -- or there could be situations where control, i.e., command and control over volunteer units could be lost and that could and will result in what he describes as serious consequences. utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

utterances.text: Yes, yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in part 2 of your report you describe the relationship between the VRS and the VJ, in particular the personal support, and you make reference to several minutes of the SDC meeting. And I just want to briefly address two of these minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we please have 65 ter 08454 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And just so we see it, we have the minutes of the 21st Session of the Supreme Defence Council held on the 7th of June, 1994. Mr. Theunens, can you tell us briefly what function the Supreme Defence Council had?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Supreme Defence Council in the FRY, so the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, which was established in May 1992, is the highest command and control organ, whereby, according to the applicable legislation, the president of the republic of the FRY commands the VJ, so the Yugoslav armed forces, in accordance with the decisions of the Supreme Defence Council which consists of the president of FRY, Serbia and Montenegro. And in the context of my report, we can see that the SDC decides about the provision, the general principles of the provision of support, be it personnel, logistics, or other support, by the VJ to the VRS as well as the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 42 in the English and page 32 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, here General Perisic is addressing his colleagues in the council. If you look at the bottom he starts speaking about the -- both presidents. And if you -- if we have the next page, please, in the English. And if you read through the first paragraph as it is continuing here, what is Mr. -- General Perisic addressing here in relation to the two other entities?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Perisic, as the Chief of the General Staff of the VJ, states that both presidents, and that means Milan Martic as president of the RSK and Mr. Karadzic as president of the RS, cannot wage war longer without the assistance of FRY, i.e., since Perisic is saying it, of the VJ. utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we now briefly have page 51 in the English and page 38 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF

And in relation to the documentation that you had available, Mr. Theunens, did you see similar figures of support in personnel reflected?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours, and without going into too many details we can see that in particular after August 1993, i.e., after General Perisic takes up the position as command -- as Chief of General Staff of the VJ, that the support, personnel, and logistics by the VJ to the VRS and the SVK becomes more systematic. Procedures are established and there are also regular reports as to the nature, both in quality and quantity of the support, that is provided by the VJ to the VRS and the SVK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document, but I have actually found that only the pages 1 and 39 through to the end are relevant to our case. And in the B/C/S it would be page 1 and 29 to the end. I don't know whether you would prefer to just admit these pages or the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, since you mentioned the relevance of this document, could you remind me how this is relevant to the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we see and what we have to deal with is that there is a constant support and payment of the -- of certain VRS officials by the -- the FRY. And at the moment, having no real -- having no proper Defence pre-trial brief, we do not know whether at some point in time Mr. Karadzic may raise that issue and make it a command and control issue. This is why we want to address it. At the same time, we also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't think I follow in full. How this is relevant to the issue of command and control, could you explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the Prosecution at the moment, we think that even if someone is paid by a -- a different entity, there is no issue of command and control. But we do not know whether it may arise in the Defence case, and we think that we have to address these matters, therefore. And in addition, we also have always said there is an overarching JCE, including personality from Belgrade, both on the political level and also on the military level; and this is why we want to show in this document how the leaderships, both the military and the political leadership of the FRY and of Serbia, basically relate to the leadership in the -- in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the RS. Therefore, we think it's quite relevant to show their constant co-operation in this way. As you can see from the minutes, that there are demands coming from the -- from Bosnia-Herzegovina, from the RS, to the FRY and Serbia; and they are responded to with certain measures and they are actually explained in this particular document. I think we have also already admitted through Mr. Treanor certain SDC minutes so far --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I just wanted to be clear as to the Prosecution's case. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I note that in paragraphs 11 and 12 of the indictment when they define the joint criminal enterprise, it includes Slobodan Milosevic, Jovica Stanisic, and other people from Serbia. So I would agree that this is relevant within what's been charged in the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you -- you have no objection to the admitting of part of this SDC document as suggested?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, page 1 and pages 39 to the end will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3048, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I have one more of these SDC minutes, Your Honour, and that's -- I would like to have 65 ter 06262 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is the minutes of the 31st Session of the SDC of 18 January 1995. Mr. Theunens, did you have an opportunity to review this document when you prepared for the testimony?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I would just like to have page 14 in the English and page 12 in the B/C/S. And we see here Mr. Milosevic saying: "The Army of Republika Srpska did not act as a factor which would make any internal pressure in order to find a peaceful solution. On the contrary, I think they are behaving quite irrationally at this" point "even from the military point of view." Mr. Theunens, from the military point of view why could one consider the behaviour of the VRS at that point in time irrational?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not specifically addressed that aspect in my report, but from my knowledge based on my professional experience prior to joining the OTP as well as when I learned when working for the OTP in the ICTY. We are January 1995. By then the president of Serbia, Mr. Milosevic, has, between quotation marks, lost his patience with the Bosnian Serbs. And he has, among other things, in August 1994 imposed sanctions against the Bosnian Serbs to punish them for their refusal of the Contact Group Peace Plan, and this is what is discussed later on with the 50/50 -- mentioning of the 50/50 solution. Contact Group Peace Plan consisted of giving 49 per cent of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the Bosnian Serbs and 51 to the Federation of Muslims or Bosniaks and Bosnian Croats. Now, the military point of view, it is generally accepted that even if the VRS did not fully reach or implement the six strategic goals at any time in conflict, in the -- during the conflict, it is still generally accepted that by the end of 1992 the VRS had gained most of the terrain it had wanted to gain and after that -- became more and more of a defensive force which would only launch attacks or counter-attacks when they felt that the ABiH or, at certain instance, the HVO were weakened at certain points. But again, by end of 1992, the most significant territorial gains have been made. Of course, the enclaves are established in spring 1993. Other examples are progress in August 1993 in the vicinity of Sarajevo, but that has to be given up following pressure by the international community. We discussed the situation in Gorazde March/April 1994. There's also the counter-offensive or counter-attacks by the VRS in the Bihac area in November 1994, but these are -- these operations are of less significance compared to the territorial gains the VRS managed to make between spring 1992 and the end of 1992. So in January 1995, Mr. Milosevic, again, making a statement as a politician, who wants the sanctions, the international sanctions against FRY to be lifted, he knows that an acceptance of a peace agreement by the Bosnian Serbs is the main precondition imposed by the international community to lift the sanctions against FRY. He tries to convince the Bosnian Serbs to accept a peaceful solution, and that's why he states that from a military point of view since the VRS has actually not made any significant gains anymore after end of 1992 or, say, early 1993, there is no military reason to continue the conflict. And from the political point of view, obviously there is the peace plan of the Contact Group that was presented in August -- excuse me, in July/August 1994 and which was accepted -- or at least Mr. Milosevic was in favour of that peace plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And if we just move to page 45 in the English and 40 in the B/C/S. And just very briefly we have Zoran Lilic speaking about the -- again, about the support, personnel support, provided to the VRS. Zoran Lilic is who?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zoran Lilic was the president of FRY at that time, so he was also presiding the SDC at least de jure.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document, and again the relevant sections are basically from page 14 in the English and page 12 in the B/C/S. The rest is not of relevance to this case here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll admit only page 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, it's actually page 14 to -- through to the end. Because the -- these pages deal with the support provided to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3049, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I note the time, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. We'll take a break for 25 minutes and resume at three past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, today you have already twice mentioned the combat-readiness report from March 1993, and I would like to have this document, D00325, be brought up on the screen. And just for the orientation, this report is mentioned throughout part 2 of the report. It's footnote 40, 69 through to 73, 936 through to 939, and 1054 through to 1056. Mr. Theunens, what is the relevance of this particular document in relation to Mr. Karadzic's authority vis-a-vis the military?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the report -- excuse me, the analysis of the combat-readiness presents a detailed analysis of the creation as well as the current status of the VRS in all aspects that are relevant for the functioning of an armed force. As for Mr. Karadzic, he signs two, call it annexes. They are not identified as annexes, but two parts at the end of the analysis of the combat-readiness. One includes the findings, and that can be found on English page 152, which is -- which are basically the conclusions of the analysis. And then on page 154 in English, Mr. Karadzic as the supreme commander of the armed forces of Republika Srpska also sets or confirms the tasks set in the analysis task and activities for the Army of Republika Srpska, i.e., the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 7 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you look at paragraph 5 counted from the top, what does it -- and it -- what -- it starts with "during the past year ...," what does it reflect in relation to the command structure of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this paragraph confirms that the VRS has been under single command and control, even if initially - and that refers to what I mentioned earlier - that is, that the transformation of what remains of the 2nd Military District, i.e., what is not withdrawn from Bosnia-Herzegovina in May 1992 together with the Bosnian Serb TO as well as other armed groups -- the transformation of these armed formations into the VRS in some parts of the territory controlled by the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina takes more time than was initially envisaged, i.e. -- and that is reported, for example, in summer 1992 by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if you move on to the next paragraph, there is a reference to the co-operation with the authorities, the SDS, and the Serbian Orthodox Church. Did you see this reflected in the documentation you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did, in particular for what the role of the SDS is concerned in establishing Bosnian Serb armed forces, i.e., Bosnian Serb Territorial Defence in various parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina in spring 1992, i.e., prior to May 1992. And then I have a section in the report where I refer to various documents from the Main Staff as well as Mr. Karadzic and subordinate units throughout the conflict, where they refer to contacts or relations with the Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 10 in the English and page 11 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in the last paragraph on page 10 there is a reference to the two periods, the first to be from April -- 1st of April to 15 June 1992 and it states, and I quote: "... an important development in the first period was the self-organising of municipal and other regional units on the basis of Territorial Defence units under the political and patriotic influence of the Serbian Democratic Party." Mr. Theunens, would that be a correct assessment based on what you, yourself, saw in the documentation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the documents I reviewed, I conclude that the expression "self-organising" is an understatement because the documents actually show that the SDS plays a leading role in organising Bosnian Serb what they call defence structures, i.e., Bosnian Serb TO in various municipalities. It may well be that there are calls from authorities in certain municipalities to establish such structures, but it is the SDS, again based on the documents I reviewed, that provides the weapons as well as the guidance as to how they should organise themselves and what kind of relations they should establish with the JNA. And just to illustrate, I can refer to minutes of an Assembly session of the 27th of March, 1992, during which -- or excuse me, according to which Mr. Karadzic calls the municipalities -- sorry, Bosnian Serb municipalities to establish Crisis Staffs in order to create also local Serb or Bosnian Serb TO units, which should subordinate themselves to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now please have page 13 in the English and page 13 also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Under the header "Infantry units" there is a reference again to the early period and the infantry units with Crisis Staffs and references to Crisis Staffs and similar authoritative bodies. And it further states that "some developed into 'paramilitary formations.'" And then further on it mentions that units were incorporated into the VRS and there is also a particular reference made to units of the former JNA. Can you explain this process that is described here and whether that is a correct description of how it went?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the purpose of my report I focused my analysis on those parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina controlled by the Bosnian Serbs which do not correspond with the so-called ARK, which was the Autonomous Region of Krajina, nor the Srebrenica area. So I didn't look at those two but I looked at the other areas. And we see in particular during take-over operations in northern Bosnia-Herzegovina between, say, April and May 1992 that various armed groups appear, but it's not always clear whether the members originate from those particular municipalities or from Serbia. There are also armed groups from Serbia, there are local Serb TO units, TO units from Serbia who are participating depending on the municipality, as well as units of the JNA. And we see then and again, that is discussed in detail in the report, that after the take-over, sometimes some of these groups create problems, problems consisting of crimes against Serbs or non-Serbs. We also see that after the establishment of the VRS, several orders are issued both by Mr. Karadzic as well as by General Mladic on the subordination of what is described as paramilitary or volunteer groups under the VRS. Now, just to end my answer, of course paramilitary formations, we need to be careful with the definition. "Paramilitary" can stand for legal units who are not part of the military but who are organised in a military manner to conduct a military task. This is not what we are talking about here. We are talking about what I would call the second significance of "paramilitary" forces or groups, that is, that illegal groups who use military means and who are organised in the military manner to achieve certain goals.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: As you already explained this term now, we also find the term used "paramilitary groups" and "volunteer groups". Is there a difference between those?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in my report I have -- for example, when discussing the reports by General Kukanjac, commander of the 2nd Military District, reports he issues in -- for example, on the 20th of March, 1992, he uses "paramilitary groups" when he talks about armed groups created by the non-Serbs, i.e., the Muslims or Bosniaks and the Bosnian Croats, whereas for similar groups on the Serbian side he tends to use the expression "volunteer groups." Now, I mean, I can give you the whole background or legal background to volunteers. Again, that's found in the report. The most important to know is that the initial concept of volunteers as it existed in the concept of All People's Defence, at least how it was implemented through the 1982 All People's Defence law, did not foresee the creation of volunteer groups. According to the legislation of 1982 and subsequent legislation - and with "subsequent" I mean until the conflict in Croatia - volunteers consists of individuals who had no military obligations but who decided to join the defence efforts and they could join the Territorial Defence, because the Territorial Defence would include all armed formations that were not part of the JNA, in order to participate in the defence of the country. It's only later, in the course of 1991, that the legal meaning of the concept of volunteer is widened in order to include also groups, and that again is explained in part of 1 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be sufficient, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And on the top -- on the top in the second paragraph there is a reference to the arming of the infantry units. Any comments from you on this particular sentence here.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have discussed that earlier. It refers to the efforts also to the SDS and the JNA to provide weapons to these units.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we now have page 69 in the English and page 62 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if you look at the second paragraph and the third paragraph, we again have here the distinction between the two periods and a reference to the JNA units withdrawn from Slovenia and Croatia to the BH, and we have a reference to the TO. Did you see what is described here reflected also in other documentation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. For the first paragraph we refer to -- I mean the second paragraph on this page, I have included information in the second part of my report on the withdrawal of some of the JNA units from Slovenia and Croatia to parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina with a Serbian majority or a significant Serb, i.e., Bosnian Serb presence. I don't mean by this that all the units from Slovenia and Croatia were withdrawn to there but at least a number of them, and there are specific withdrawal orders for that. Yes, and the third paragraph on the creation of the TO we have addressed that -- the creation of the Bosnian Serb TO with -- where it is stated here, the leadership of the SDS that -- I mean, organised and planned the creation of these units and also instructed them to be subordinated to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. If you look at the third-last paragraph on this page in the English, there is a reference to the withdrawal of the JNA as -- and it's mentioned here "FRY army," as it is said here. And I quote: "The pull-out of most of the combat hardware together with the personnel," that is, "FRY nationals was prevented." What does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this refers to the withdrawal or the official withdrawal of the JNA from Bosnia-Herzegovina during May 1992, whereby the VRS can benefit from the weapons and infrastructure and ammunition and other logistics supplies from JNA units that were deployed in Bosnian Serb-controlled territory prior to the withdrawal. We have also seen - and I have not addressed that in detail but I think I have one or two documents under that - that already prior to May the JNA in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 2nd Military District, redeploys, for example, ammunition and other logistical storages from parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina without a significant Serb presence or with a Croatian or Muslim majority to parts with a Serbian majority. I mentioned already the withdrawal from Slovenia and Croatia. And those storages and weapons are then available to the VRS when the JNA officially withdraws from Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 153 in the English displayed and 133 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you have already referred to the concluding remarks signed by Mr. Karadzic in the beginning, and I would just want to ask you one additional question in relation to paragraph 4. And it says here -- it refers to the relation to the command -- how does it refer to the relation -- command and control of the VRS and relationship between the military and civilian authority and situational awareness?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, the two paragraphs under heading 4 confirm that the principles of command and control, the three principles as they are defined in the 1982 SFRY All People's Defence law, namely, single authority, unity of command, and the obligation to implement decisions, that these principles are implemented also in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the RS subsequently in 1992. And the paragraph then explains the relationship between the Supreme Command and the Main Staff, whereby the Main Staff acts as the staff of the Supreme Command, which is also consistent with the structure that existed in the SFRY, where there was a Supreme Command and the Supreme Command Staff during one of the three states: State of war, imminent threat of war, or state of emergency.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have page 154 in the English and page 134 in the B/C/S on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, you have already mentioned that Mr. Karadzic signed another part of the combat-readiness report setting out the tasks, and we do not need to go into details, further details, here. Just one question in relation to the second part of point 3, where it says: "Co-operation should be organised in the zones of war operations with the authorities, the MUP, and the Serbian Orthodox Church at all levels of control and command, and should be considered an integral part of the modern control and command." Can you please tell us why this would be an integral part of control and command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have to see that in the context of how the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina operated, and subsequently the Republika Srpska. And, again, for me it's an implementation of the principle of unified command and control, that is, that all organs of the state - and, okay, we add here the Serbian Orthodox Church because of the moral importance it plays for the Bosnian Serbs - that they all act in the same direction in order to implement the goals set by the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Now I would like to have page 158 in the English and 138 in the B/C/S. And there is a chapter called: "Basic characteristics of the operational-tactical utilisation of the Army of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: What is laid out in this particular section of the combat-readiness report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this part is actually a summary of the report and it also includes some of the views expressed -- or some of the conclusions, better, conclusions expressed by Mr. Karadzic that describe how the VRS was used, i.e., how it implemented the goals set by the Supreme Command, supreme commander, and how the VRS was created, including also how it operated in order to implement these goals.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document we have already admitted. Can we --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In relation to the early period spring 1992, I would like to address two more documents with you, Mr. Theunens, and the first can we have 65 ter 00147 on the screen. And as it is coming up, these are the minutes of a joint meeting of the National Security Council and the Government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina of the 15th of April, 1992. Mr. Theunens, there is under item -- under item 1 a reference to daily meetings and under item -- yeah, reference to daily meetings. And under item 3 the proposal to declare a state of imminent threat of war. And can we have the next page, please, in both languages. And there is mentioned a decision, that the minister of defence shall organise and supervise the TO until the appointment of the commander. Mr. Theunens, does this document reflect on the authority over the armed units at that time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours -- I mean, the -- maybe first, a short introduction. The National Security Council is established by the Bosnian Serbs 27th of March, 1992, is intended as an advisory body for political security and other relevant matters that apply according to the National Security Council to the security or the safety of the Bosnian Serbs. I have discussed a number of minutes of meetings or reports of meetings in my report where I basically state or conclude that the Council for National Security also decides on matters dealing with defence, even if I have seen no indication that it is a command and control body. To answer the question of Ms. Uertz, yeah, here it is decided to appoint an acting commander of the TO as well as the Chief of Staff of the TO -- meaning the Serb-established Bosnian Serb TO. And then also instructions are given to the minister of defence on organising and supervising, whereby supervising stands more for managing than for actual command and control of the Territorial Defence. Because as we know from other documents, command and control is established in the field, and according to the applicable legislation and guide-lines from the SFRY armed forces which were also used by the Bosnian Serbs at that stage, the TO should be under the command of the JNA if they operate in the same area.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Elliott just informed me that this document was admitted in the bar table decision of yesterday but I wouldn't know the number now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The number will be assigned in due course. It hasn't been but let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, I have another document and Ms. Elliott also informed me that this document is also part of the bar table submission of yesterday. Can we have 65 ter 150 -- 00150 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, this document is cited in footnote 146 and 1048 of the second part of the report, and I also forgot to mention that the previous document was also mentioned in several footnotes in the -- in the report of Mr. Theunens. But in relation to this document that we see now, the minutes of another session of the National Security Council and the government, looking at item 2 it says here "military commanding," can you explain what, according to this document, Mr. Karadzic's role is in relation to the TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my conclusion in the context of the other documents I reviewed is that Mr. Karadzic is to co-ordinate, i.e., to harmonise - as it is officially defined in SFRY armed forces doctrine when discussing the concept of co-ordination - harmonise the use of the TO together with the JNA. And this probably refers to meetings mentioned by General Kukanjac in his report of 20th of March, meetings between the command of the 2nd Military District and the SDS. And of course, as we know from other documents I discuss in my report, members of the SDS or in particular Mr. Karadzic in early 1992 also participate in meetings of what remains of the SFRY Presidency where also high-level issues on command and control of Serb forces in the field and their relation with the JNA are being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff, instead of leaving this pending we can admit it and give the number now and we can make of course a reference when the admitting -- giving numbers that was admitted --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- through bar table motions.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. That would mean that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The previous one --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Needs to get a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, will be exhibited as P3050. And this one, 150, will be admitted as Exhibit P3051.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I would now like to have 65 ter 08450 be brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we had discussed the directive number 6 already this morning, and now we have a, as it says, supplement -- supplement to directive number 6 to the SRK signed by General Mladic on the 14th of December, 1993. And on page 1 in the beginning there is a reference made to the decision reached by the highest officials of the Serbian people, and then there is mention reinforcement forces -- in this group of participating forces there is mentioned reinforcement forces of the VJ special forces. Mr. Theunens, when troops of the VJ are joining the SRK as reinforcement forces, who would then be in command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the use of the terminology "reinforcement" as well as the context of this specific order indicates that these forces of the VJ are subordinated to the commander in the field, i.e., the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we have the next page, please, it's -- the B/C/S is the same, but in English it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And we have here a reference to -- it's under point 3 a little bit further down, special forces of the MUP participation. If -- when special forces of the MUP are joining such an operation, who would be in charge -- in command of these troops?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we have to look at the specific contents of the order. I know that in the -- in the VRS there was a general -- um -- I think an instruction or a guide-line that states that when police and VRS operate in the same area, then police should be subordinate to the VRS. Now, when we look at this order and we look at the heading paragraph 3, it specifically states that a number of forces are resubordinated to you, i.e., the commander of the SRK. And the special forces of the MUP are, together with the VJ units we mentioned earlier, are part of these forces, i.e., forces that are resubordinated to the command of the SRK, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I forgot to mention that this particular document is mentioned in footnote 368, 620, 622, and 871. And I would like to have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3052, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 15274 on the screen. And, Your Honour, it is mentioned in footnote 943 of the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what are we looking at here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order by Mr. Karadzic, supreme commander of the VRS. Now, I just want to mention, I couldn't -- and, okay, we have the original B/C/S because the translation comes from a book by Mr. Karadzic or somebody who compiled a book with various orders issued by Mr. Karadzic, but, okay, for the B/C/S we are fine. And basically it's issued on the 7th of February, 1994, and it refers specifically to the Sarajevo situation, which we can derive or we can conclude that from the addressees, not only the Main Staff of the VRS but also the commander of the SRK and the brigade commanders of the SRK.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And what does it show about the situational awareness of the supreme commander of what was going on in Sarajevo at that time in -- on the 7th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, in the order he signs, shows that he is aware of, and I will quote, "proof that the Serb side response to Muslim artillery provocation are inadequate, sometimes 20 to 30, even 70 times more massive." So it shows that he is aware of this. Now it could be that he has been made aware by international mediators who are in regular contact with him or through VRS reporting, that we cannot establish.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in relation to the order that he then issues, any further comments by you? And we can also look at the end of -- on the next page in the English where there is point 3 mentioned.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Paragraphs 1 and 2 he -- Mr. Karadzic orders to keep or to introduce, as he calls it, the strictest control on the use of artillery as a means of retaliation to what he calls provocations. The third paragraph could be considered unusual because Mr. Karadzic orders the corps artillery, i.e., the artillery assets of the corps -- or, I'm sorry, I need to correct that. He -- he actually states that the corps commanders for the use of the corps artillery, i.e., the artillery assets of the corps, are directly responsible to him, where one would expect that they are responsible to the command of the Main Staff and that the command of the Main Staff would be responsible to him. Now, it -- my conclusion would be that this -- this very strong order, and also the fact that he directly orders the commanders of the corps, is related to the specific situation in Sarajevo and the date of this order, 7th of February, i.e., a few days after the incident known as the Markale market shelling. And I think it's also relevant to mention paragraph 4, that: "Every incident has to be reported to me." Re-affirming the supreme commander's will and actually clear instructions that he is informed of all events.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the origin of this document? It's -- are they all excerpts from a book?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This particular one is an excerpt from a book, but I know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Particular one being what --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The English one?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Both --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Both are excerpts from a book.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: From a book. But, I think, Mr. Theunens in his report refers to that same document but he has the -- the actual order. I seem to recall that, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- but may -- Mr. Theunens may perhaps know better than me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I was just wondering if we might send this to translation. I'm not sure exactly about the translation. Just from my own looking - I don't know Serbian - but where they say, "the proofs that the Serb side response is inadequate sometimes being 20 or 30 or even 70 times more massive," I'm not really sure if that's been accurately translated or not. So I was thinking maybe it would be more prudent to send this back for the language section to translate the Serbian into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The document that is appearing on the monitor is the wrong one. There are two pages. If you note the date, this is not the identical one. We can show the other side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the document in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is it? Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The B/C/S page -- has two documents, contains two documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We do -- we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any problem in admitting it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3053, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now please have 65 ter 01914 be brought up on the screen. And, Your Honour, this document is mentioned in the report under footnotes 1059, 1061, and 1062.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up here, Mr. Theunens, what do we see here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an example of a regular combat report, a daily combat report, by the Main Staff of the VRS dated the 12th of July, 1995, and sent to the regular addressees, i.e., the president; as well as the commanders of the VRS corps and equivalent units.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
