utterances.text: Can we please have the next -- the third page in the English, and it would be the third page also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And if you could comment on the task or the details of the Drina Corps when it comes to description of the enemy and the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, the report for each of the VRS corps provides an overview of the operations conducted during the last 24 hours. And for the Drina Corps, I mean, it's explained on 6(a) and (b). Under (a) we have the situation with the enemy, under (b) the situation in the corps, whereby -- it is stated here combat operations tasks are going ahead as planned and these are the combat tasks that fall under Operation Krivaja 95. Mention is made of addition of liberation of Potocari --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, that's on the top of page 4. And then it also mentions, on a number of axes, that part of the Drina Corps units and MUP units have organised ambushes in order to destroy -- or what is described as Muslim extremists who have not surrendered and who are trying to break out from the enclave towards Tuzla. Furthermore, I mean, on page 4 there's also situation in the territory that falls within the area of responsibility or the area of operations of the Drina Corps, where the transport of population -- the organised transport of population from Srebrenica towards Kladanj is addressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. That should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I request the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3054, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can I now ask Exhibit 65 ter 04199 be brought up on the screen, please. And, Your Honour, this document is mentioned in footnote 165 and 247.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is an order by the Birac Brigade command to the Zvornik TO staff of the 28th of May, 1992. Mr. Theunens, in relation to the various orders related to the TO, what does it show in relation to command and control?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an example of the situation I spoke about earlier, that is, that after the establishment of the VRS, which is officially announced at the Assembly session of the Bosnian Serbs that is held on the 12th of May, 1992, and then as we discussed earlier there is the 15th of June decision on the structure and command and control of the VRS, that is, that during the time-period in some parts of the territory controlled by the Bosnian Serbs there are some difficulties to integrate those TO -- the Bosnian Serb TO units into the newly established VRS. And this is an example of an order by a VRS officer to subordinate and to integrate the Zvornik TO, Bosnian Serb TO, into the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, looking at point 6: "The moving out of the Muslim population ..." and the placing of men fit for military service in camps. Any comments on this from your side?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we know from the context from the Bosnian Serb take-over of Zvornik which occurred earlier in May, that this take-over was accompanied by movements of population, more specifically of non-Serbs. And -- I mean, mainly Muslims, excuse me, and this is covered here -- I mean, the way how this has to be conducted, how these Muslims have to be moved out is explained in this paragraph 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request the admission of this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit P3055.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in -- as well -- in part 1 of your report and also part 2 you have particular chapters on the various volunteers and paramilitaries, and in both parts of your report you refer to Arkan and his Serbian Volunteer Guard. And in this context I would like to show you one document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we please have 65 ter 05274 be brought up on the screen. And, Your Honour, it's mentioned in footnote 1150 of the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And as it is coming up, it is a dispatch to the RS MUP attaching a request by General Mladic to both the RS president and the MUP of 23rd September, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have the next page in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be 1995, the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, 1995, right. I misspoke. Mr. Theunens, looking at the two first paragraphs, what are General Mladic's observations regarding the control over Arkan and his men?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic in this letter to Mr. Karadzic, as well as the RS Ministry of the Interior, states that Arkan and his men are active in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps, that they are not part of any formation unit, i.e., they are not part of any VRS unit. So they are not subordinated to any VRS unit. They are not getting -- receiving assignments from the VRS. So the conclusion of Mr. Mladic -- of General Mladic is that they are paramilitary formations acting independently of the VRS. And then in the second paragraph General Mladic describes or mentions that Arkan has received an enactment, so a kind of authorisation or a decision from the president of the RS, Dr. Karadzic, empowering Arkan to "bring in, question, incarcerate, and escort all men fit for the military except for Assembly deputies and members of the RS MUP." And according to Mladic, this in practice has been limited to abuse of VRS members, especially high-ranking officers. And then he gives further details of the activities of Arkan and his Volunteer Guards.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And in paragraph 4 of the same page there's a reference also -- what does he state about the behaviour of Arkan's troops towards local Muslim population in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to General Mladic, Arkan's paramilitary units, they have arrested all the Muslims in Sanski Most and liquidated a certain number of loyal Muslims, including family members of some VRS servicemen. That's what he writes about the activities about -- of Arkan and his men against Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And then it is -- basically he requests the RS -- the president of the RS to -- to revoke his decision to empower Arkan, disarm them, and so on and so forth. And on the next page in the English, please, also refers -- requests the MUP to actively stop this. To your knowledge, did the RS president stop Arkan and did the MUP intervene, do you know?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, I don't know. I know that Arkan left -- and his men left eventually, but I don't know the circumstances, whether or not this was linked to any instructions issued by Mr. Karadzic. I have not seen any documents on those circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The view that General Mladic has here on this particular group, paramilitary group, did you see this reflected in other military documentation as well? I mean not just Arkan, but other volunteer and paramilitary groups, do you know whether they also have a quite critical view on these troops?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There is the report General Tolimir compiles on 28th of July, 1992, on paramilitary groups. In this report Tolimir, as assistant commander for intelligence and security, shares with President Karadzic as well as General Mladic and other senior military officers, I mean members of the Main Staff, includes a very critical view, very negative view, of various paramilitary, i.e., volunteer, groups operating on the territory controlled by the Bosnian Serbs. It talks about their lack of combat value, their -- the fact that they are inclined or prone to commit crimes against Serbs and non-Serbs. And this Tolimir report is then used as a basis for orders issued by the Main Staff to subordinate or remove these volunteers. There's also an order - and I think it's even from earlier, is it from May or June 1992 - by Mr. Karadzic as President of the Presidency of the SRBiH to subordinate these groups to the VRS or have them removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: According to the military documentation that you reviewed, were such volunteer or paramilitary groups part of the VRS or the TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, I have not looked at the situation in the Autonomous Region of Krajina nor at the situation in Eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina. I focused on Northern Bosnia-Herzegovina and Sarajevo, and there we see that, for example, during some of the take-over operations - and for the specifics I would like to refer to my report - that some volunteer groups are identified as TO units, local Serb TO units or they are part of local Serb TO units or they are co-operating with them under the instructions of the Crisis Staff. Now, for the VRS, Sarajevo is a good example in the sense that we know - and this is discussed in the report - that there are various groups that are affiliated to the Serbian Radical Party. And these groups - I mean, the key members - over time there is documentation that indicates that they are members of the Bosnian Serb MUP and other times they are members of the VRS by, for example, the group -- I'm just thinking now of the group of Vaske, for example, has a military post number and is identified as a kind of a special intervention detachment of the VRS unit of the SRK, Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and that also applies to other SRS-affiliated volunteer groups operating in the Sarajevo area after May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. You just mentioned that earlier on Mr. Karadzic also made decisions in relation to the -- these groups.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we please have 65 ter 15367 be brought up. Your Honour, I forgot to mention that we -- I want like -- would like to have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the previous document, 5274, will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3056, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, that's not correct. 15367. The B/C/S is correct but the document is not -- please, the next page, next page. Next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what are we looking at here? Is that the decision that you referred to or ... ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This is -- I mean, I mentioned May or June 1992. It's actually 13th of June, 1992. A decision by Mr. Karadzic, President of the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as a text, I mean it's clear, putting a ban on formation and operations of armed groups of the -- the English says unique, but it should be single control or authority of the VRS or -- "milicija" stands actually for the forces of the Ministry of the Interior, i.e., the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have this admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The English itself is an original document?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3057, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have 65 ter 13375 be brought up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are waiting, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, can I ask you how much longer would you need for the purpose of planning.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would think another five minutes because I have only this document and one more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we have here an announcement on the arrest of outlaws signed by Mr. Karadzic of 6 August 1992. What you see here in this announcement, does this reflect on the authority of the Presidency and the accused and what stance does Mr. Karadzic and the Presidency take?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this announcement of the arrest follows from the previous order or decision, that is, that groups that are not subordinated to the VRS -- or that do not want to subordinate to the VRS but operate independently and who have committed crimes, that there he uses his authority -- I mean Mr. Karadzic uses his authority to have them arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Exhibit P3058.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in part 2 of your report you describe the VRS military discipline and military justice system, and you -- in footnote 345 you mention that Mr. Karadzic on the 17th of June, 1992, signed a decree establishing a state documentation centre for investigation of war crimes against Serb people. As this is described in your report, we do not need to pull it up, but do you know whether a documentation centre existed gathering information on war crimes against non-Serbs on RS territory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, from the documents I have reviewed, I have not come across such documentation centre. The documents I have seen refer to crimes committed against Serbs. And as I mentioned just to be, I mean, complete in my answer, I have not reviewed anything or any documentation related to the situation in the Autonomous Region of Krajina, but elsewhere from the documents I have reviewed the gathering of information is focused or is actually limited to crimes against Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can we please have P02646 on the screen. And, Your Honour, this is mentioned in footnote 354. And as it is coming up, it is a request of Colonel Lugonja of the SRK intelligence and security department dated 17 May 1995 to all units, referring to a meeting of the government commission for gathering data on war crimes against humanity and international law.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what does Colonel Lugonja ask the SRK units under his command to do?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asks them - and he asks more specifically the chief of the security organs of the SRK units and that is explained in the second paragraph, to gather all the data and evidence in the zones of these units on war crimes, crimes against humanity and international law committed by the enemy against the Serbs and Serbian people on the territory of the RS and the former Bosnia-Herzegovina under Muslim and Croatian control.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, this concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I want to tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This has been already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karadzic, please start your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good afternoon to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens. Please don't hold it against me if I'm mispronouncing your last name. It's not easy for you either with all of our last names.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karadzic. I try my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the break I would like to put a few general questions. You worked in the Office of the Prosecutor from 2001 until 2009 as an investigator or analyst? What would you call it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I worked during the time-period mentioned by Mr. Karadzic as an analyst, and more specifically the official job title was intelligence analyst (military). That was my official job title.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that you were involved in collecting and analysing documents that pertained to my role in the capacity of supreme commander of the Territorial Defence of the Serb Republic of BiH and afterwards the Republika Srpska army as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you establish that I did have a role as supreme commander of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that there was no official title or as -- I mean saying supreme commander of the Territorial Defence. But I tried -- in the scope of the report, I tried to summarise the authority of Mr. Karadzic, the authority both as -- I mean, in the positions he held between early 1992 and November 1995 in relation to the armed forces of the Bosnian Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then you said that the point of the first part of the report is to present the legal and doctrinary framework and so on and so forth within the SFRY armed forces and the VJ and also volunteer-paramilitary formations from Serbia and the local forces in Croatia with a special emphasis on command and control and alleged violations of laws and customs of war; right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not have an exact reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, that is explained in the scope and methodology of the report, and Mr. Karadzic is referring to paragraph 2(a) of that scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So I should be certain that you looked at all the aspects of the activity of the Serb regular forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina within a proper context, since this chapter is called "context"; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not sure I understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I can repeat it. This paragraph, 2(a), says that the first part is entitled "context." And later on you also repeat -- or actually, during the examination-in-chief you said yesterday if something needs to be done it has to be placed within context. Can I count on you having viewed the existence and activity of the regular forces of the Serbs in Croatia within an appropriate context?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not used the expression "regular forces of Serbs in Croatia" in my report. I talk about the forces established by the Serbs in Croatia, TO of the SAO Krajina and the SAO SBWS which is transformed into RSK TO. We also have a police force which is known as milicija. This is then transformed under the Vance Plan into the PJM, as Special Milicija Forces. And then if I remember well in the course of 1993, what was a TO and became PJM is then transformed again into SVK. That is what I have analysed and discussed in part 1 of the report in relation to Serb forces in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to wonder then, when you say "Serb forces," do you mean both regular and irregular forces, everything that was organised by the Serbs and done by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I always try to use the original names and if the term "irregular" would be used or if it was used in one of the documents I consulted, I would also use it in my report. But I don't believe that I use -- that I qualified any of the Serb forces I have identified in part 1 of the report as "regular" or "irregular." I have expressed views as to whether the PJM was in line with the Vance Plan or whether the SVK was coherent or consistent with the Vance Plan. But I don't remember specifying whether they were irregular. And I emphasize the word or the expression "irregular" or "regular."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, since your task was to study, analyse, the role of Radovan Karadzic in his capacity of supreme commander, first of all, the Territorial Defence and then the Army of Republika Srpska, do we have to decide then during this cross-examination over which forces does Radovan Karadzic have control and where does his responsibility lie? Or does Radovan Karadzic have responsibility for all Serbs who are armed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not stated anywhere in the report that Mr. Karadzic has responsibility for all Serbs who are armed, but I included the analysis of Serb forces in Croatia for at least two reasons. The first reason to provide the historical context and also to show that there are patterns. We see a pattern -- we see patterns in how these forces are established in Croatia, what they do, where they operate, and these patterns - at least based on my analysis - are repeated in Bosnia-Herzegovina or certain parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. A second reason is that - as I have explained in part 2 of the report - there is co-operation between Serbs in Croatia and Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina. For on the military level, there is at least the example of Operation Corridor in -- first May/June 1992 and then followed in November 1992, where forces of the RSK MUP, the police, operate in Bosnia-Herzegovina under the command of the VRS in order to achieve or implement a key -- the second strategic goal, namely, the establishment of a corridor between Krajina and Semberija. Later on we see another example of the -- of operational co-operation between SVK and VRS in the latter half of 1994 in the Bihac area in support of the autonomous province of Western Bosnia of Fikret Abdic. So these are just two examples explaining the military reason why I included this discussion and analysis of Serb forces as well as also, as I mentioned, the fact of the establishment of co-operation mechanisms between Serbs in Croatia and Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So these were examples of co-operation between the legal representatives of the authorities of the Serbs in Croatia and the Serbs in Bosnia, right, and the forces that are under their control; is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm -- I'm not here to express myself as to whether they are legal or non-legal representatives, but -- I mean, I have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, transcript page 92, line 2, you said: [In English] "What you will look for is the context ..." [Interpretation] This first chapter, this first part of your analysis is entitled "Context." That is why I'm asking once again: Did you manage to look at the activity and conduct of the forces that you ascribe to me, that your analysis ascribes to the Territorial Defence or the Army of Republika Srpska, did you manage to view this and analyse it in an appropriate context? Are you satisfied with what you achieved in terms of placing things into context, the one that you refer to yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Context is referring to background? Where do you find "context" in his report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it may be translation issue. I used the word "framework" or background, but maybe with the translation to B/C/S it becomes context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But yesterday during the examination-in-chief on page 92, line 2, the distinguished Mr. Theunens said: [In English] "What you will look for is the context ..." [Interpretation] So for assessing a particular phenomenon, it is necessary to place it into context. I agree with that. However, I wonder whether this analysis succeeded in viewing the phenomenon of the Serb forces that I'm supposed to be responsible for, were they analysed in context? Were they placed in context? If you are satisfied with that, say yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall I read out the passage from your evidence of yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That would be -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It reads like this: "The fact that the same information or the same facts is reported several times does not add to the credibility of the information, but it can -- it can assist. What you will look for is the context. For example, when we see information for the first time and it doesn't fit into the context, we will conduct additional searches, again applying the same methodology, in order to try -- in order to assess and establish the credibility of that information." Now you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much for the clarification. I -- I believe that this refers to another aspect of my testimony than what Mr. Karadzic is now referring to. When I spoke of context in relation -- yesterday, it was to explain the methodology I used and the specific aspect of establishing reliability of sources and credibility of information. This is something else than what Mr. Karadzic is now referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, what I read out, the point of the first part of the report entitled "background" or "context" is to present the doctrinary framework where armed forces operated, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have an exact reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I -- I mean, I mentioned that earlier. Mr. Karadzic is referring to paragraph 2(a) of the scope and methodology, where I explain the purpose of part 1 of the report. And I have attempted to explain again, with concrete examples, political co-operation as well as military co-operation as well as other aspects why I considered that relevant for the second part of the report, i.e., to provide the framework or background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The existence and the operation of the Army of Republika Srpska, the essence of its being, is that fundamentally determined by its relationship with the opponent because of which it exists?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very general question and I will give a very general answer. Opponents can play a role in determining the defence doctrine and the strategy, but you don't need to have an opponent as a precondition to establish armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. However, in order to use them you need to have an enemy; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's again a very -- a general question. I mean, you can create the enemy or the enemy can express his or her hostile intentions towards you. It all depends of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go back to that. So your work for the OTP was aimed at completing and reinforcing the indictment against me; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wouldn't agree with that proposition because it is incorrect. I mean, I -- I didn't write this report for the OTP. The OTP requested me to write a report, but I tried to the best of my capabilities to analyse, in all possible objectivity and in a professional manner, the material to which I had access. And that report was written irrespective of the indictment. I mean, the only direction I received was -- were instructions from Ms. Uertz as to which topics I should address, that's it. And on the basis of that, I compiled this report as I did -- as I did with all the other reports I drafted during my work on my professional activities for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your work in the OTP started in 2001. Is it correct that the indictment against me had already been there for five or six years?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you have a look at it? Did you familiarise yourself with it properly when you started working in the OTP?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have had a look at it much earlier, I mean when it was issued, out of interest because I was at the time -- if I remember well, I was working in Zagreb in the headquarters of UNPROFOR, but I did not use it -- or I didn't familiarise myself with it during my work at the OTP, let alone when I started to work for the OTP, because I was working on another case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when were you given this task to analyse the role of Radovan Karadzic? Did you then familiarise yourself with the existing indictment? Did you read it then?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I started to work on this report in January 2009, and I don't believe that I read the indictment then. I may have read the indictment or an earlier version of my stay here -- during my professional activities at the ICTY -- at the OTP of the ICTY. But again, I have not familiarised myself with the indictment. It is not a basis for my report. As I said, the direction came from Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff, and in the direction she referred to earlier reports I had prepared for other cases or related cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To the extent to which you had insight into this indictment, had it been completed from the point of view of your assignment? Had it been completed from the point of view of the things that you were researching?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand the question. I believe that Mr. Karadzic wants to establish a link between the indictment and my report, whether it's in time or contents, and I tried to explain in my previous answers that there is no link between the report and the indictment. As I explained, the direction I used -- sorry, the direction I received originated from Ms. -- Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff and did not refer to the indictment or did not include the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you were working for the OTP then, weren't you? It is the OTP that provided you direction and instructions, and that is part of the process that you referred to, the four stages of the process that you referred to; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- indeed, Your Honours, with the clarification that the direction, as I explained it, as the first phase in the process is -- is to say what I should do; it doesn't state how I should do it. I mean, I was requested to write a report on a particular issue, and I mean the issue is explained in the scope of the report, the first paragraph, in very general terms and I then specified it. And there was some communication with Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, but she didn't tell me what I should write. I mean, that is my job and nobody else interferes in that. I write a report on the basis of the material I review and the conclusions are based on the material I review and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time. If it is convenient, we will have a break for 50 minutes and we'll resume at 25 past 1.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From now on until the end of this week, we'll be sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis, Judge Morrison being away due to some official business. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, with all due respect, I have to establish exactly how we stand with respect to your report. You were working for the OTP for eight years. Can you tell us how they used the results of your work. What happened with what you submitted to them? Or rather, what happened to the work you did for the OTP according to the instructions given to you, in this case by Madam Uertz-Retzlaff, and in other cases from others. What did you do and what happened to those materials?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand that the question both covers my regular work as an intelligence analyst (military) as well as an analyst or an intelligence analyst (military) who was requested to draft reports, like the reports that we are discussing now, because there is a distinction between the two. It is correct that I participated in the investigation of serious crimes based on the instructions I received from my supervisors in the Office of the Prosecutor. In addition, I was also requested to draft certain reports, and these reports -- well, they were presented in the trials where I was called to testify. And then it was up to the Trial Chamber - and I emphasize the Trial Chamber - to decide what to do with the report, whether they would admit it or not. And what they would further do with it, well, that is entirely up to the discretion of the Trial Chamber and it is something the OTP has nothing -- is not involved in whatsoever. So I think it's important to make the distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly that in the course of those eight years you did work for someone else in addition to the OTP as an intelligence analyst?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's look at line 11. You say: [In English] "I understand that the question both covers my regular work as an intelligence analyst (military) as well as an analyst or an intelligence analyst (military) who was requested to draft reports, like the reports ..." and so on. [Interpretation] What were the two kinds of work that you did?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat my answer and I apologise if it wasn't clear. My regular work for the Office of the Prosecutor consists of providing analytical support during investigations and during trials. And if you want, I can go into detail about that. I make a distinction with the report because the intervention or the role of the OTP in the preparation of the report is limited to giving me the direction, i.e., to determine the topic I should analyse and I should write a report about. Of course I have access to the databases and the material that is available to the Office of the Prosecutor. Before the report would be filed, I would send a draft report to the team that had given me the initial tasking. In certain cases - and I'm not talking about this case, but again other cases during my stay here - several drafts were sent over time. There would have -- there could have been a discussion about certain drafts in the sense that I didn't fully address topics that the Office of the Prosecutor requested me to address or maybe I went into too much detail about a certain issue. The report would then be finalised and it would be filed by the Office of the Prosecutor -- okay, by the team I was -- excuse me, that requested me to compile the report. It would be filed as -- on the -- would be put on the 65 ter list. And then they would call me as a witness, whereby, as I mentioned earlier, it would be up to the Trial Chamber to determine whether the report would be admitted or not and also to see further on what they would do with the report for their activities in relation to the specific trial. So the point I'm trying to emphasize is that there is a distinction between the two types of activities in a sense that obviously in the regular work I get feedback from the Office of the Prosecutor on the small projects I was dealing with, but the -- as for the compilation of, call it expert reports, there the role of the OTP is limited to providing the first -- providing the initial direction. Then eventually providing feedback as to whether my drafts have addressed the topics that were covered by this direction. And then, of course as I would call the matter of logistics, is to submit the report as part of the 65 ter list in order for the Trial Chamber to decide on its further use.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is very exhaustive and very useful. Thank you very much. Now let me see whether I understood you correctly. The OTP did not use your findings to draft an indictment. So the indictment was not adapted to your findings, but on the contrary your findings were adapted to the thesis put forward in the counts of the indictment; and that's why your several drafts were submitted and what they were used for. Is that correct? In other words, when the draft of your report fulfils the expectations of the OTP, it is finalised and it goes on to the 65 ter list. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, that's not really what I tried to explain, but I can try a third time. I worked here eight years. In some cases indictments were available before, later -- anyway, anything is possible. Whether the OTP uses my draft for whatever purpose, I don't know. They don't give me a briefing like it would be in a command and control structure, like to report to me like we have done this and this with your draft. I would say, "Is there a problem," whatever they do with it. But I can assure you - and I'm talking now about -- I think I did six or seven reports - that the OTP never interfered with the contents of the report except maybe in one case, and I can explain it if you want -- and again it's not this report with linguistical issues. I am not a native speaker. No, the OTP did not tell me to change the contents of a draft report except maybe to expand on an issue or to include another issue, but they never ever told me what I should write. And again, what they did with my drafts or whether they used it for indictments or not, I don't know. I was not consulted about that. I think you have to ask the Prosecution about that, and I hope I have clarified the matter now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to know then why they had to consider several drafts?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I gave a generic answer to covering the eight years I was working here. If -- I mean, the facts for this report, I was tasked on the 25th of January. I submitted a first draft -- no, excuse me, there was a meeting I believe on the 18th of February, where I just submitted a draft table of contents just to show, like, okay, these are the topics I want to discuss. Then I believe, if I remember well, that I had a kind of a dead-line to submit a draft report by, say, mid of March. I explained to the Office of the Prosecutor that I was not able to do so because there was so much material available, including material that had to be revised. So I may have provided a draft then, but I don't recall receiving any feedback to that draft. And after that, there was another meeting I believe around 16th or 17th -- excuse me -- yeah, that was 16th or 17th of March, a meeting where I explained that, that I couldn't meet the dead-line. Then I submitted what I would call the final draft, i.e., the final report, by the 15th of April. So this is for this specific report. Now, if you want to know for reports I did for other cases, and I mentioned that already, there may have been feedback in some cases as to the drafts of the report, but that was mainly to include additional issues or leave out certain issues or for certain linguistical matters. And I hope that that again answers the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It partially answers the question, but I'm still confused. If your report was something that the OTP needed, how come they were able to write an indictment against me without it? And if they did not need it, what did your draft report change in relation to the indictment against me?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's not for the witness to answer that question. Move on to your next topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Theunens, but the Defence has to establish whether this is a case of the OTP testifying because you are the fourth witness this month who was an employee of the OTP and is testifying as an independent expert. So I'm asking you for the sake of illustration, when, for example, it is stated that the Serbs took over power in some municipalities, and this is stated in the indictment and also in your report. I want to know whether this is something that you established by your own investigation on the ground or whether this is something you took over from the indictment and how did you come by this information, that the Serbs took over power in those municipalities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I think this has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, this is a specific question. Let's mention specific municipalities. How did Mr. Theunens come by the information that the Serbs took over power in a particular municipality? Did he establish this on the basis of documents or on the basis of his own investigations on the ground or did he simply take it as an established fact? Maybe he can answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I would invite Mr. Karadzic -- excuse me, to go to the relevant section of the report, in English it starts at page 133 and it ends -- I mean, the municipalities I have discussed, it ends on English page -- excuse me, 192. You will see that for each of the findings or conclusions or facts that I put I have a reference, and that reference is a document. And in almost all the cases this is a document that originates from those involved in the take-over operations, be it local Serb TO, Crisis Staff, JNA, forces of the Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Interior police, and it's on the basis -- I mean, that is the process I applied. It's on the basis of these primary sources, these documents, that I drew certain conclusions. It is correct that of the selection of municipalities is based on the direction I received from the Office of the Prosecutor, that is, that Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff in her first request to me to draft a report for this case referred to a report I did for the Seselj -- or the trial of Mr. Vojislav Seselj, where I had selected a number of municipalities. And Ms. -- Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff confirmed that this -- these municipalities should also be addressed in -- or should also be covered in the report here for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, let's look, for example, at what it says in the pre-trial brief, point 43. "On the same day, the 24th of March, 1992, expecting the state to be divided ..." and so on. "The preparation of a functional government was carried out." And in 44 it says, that's your report. "In the following weeks, the organs of government and the organs of the Bosnian Serbs carried out a number of forcible take-overs in certain municipalities by the holding of a 16th Session in Banja Luka ...," and then you list the municipalities which in your opinion were taken over, where the Serbs took over power in a forcible way. And in 102 you say: "Less than a week after this announcement in the evening hours on the 31st of March, 1992, the Serb Volunteer Guard, or rather, the Arkan's men and the TO forces attacked Bijeljina, killed at least 48 Muslim civilians, and took power in the town. After these Serb forces from Serbia and Bosnia took control, the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina municipality was established as the organ of government in that area." Are you trying to say that you established what happened in Bijeljina on the 31st of March and the 1st and 2nd of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I want --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I can't -- I can't find the reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what he's actually citing. Is Dr. Karadzic citing now the pre-trial brief or is he citing to the report? Definitely not to the report because I can't find that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have here 43, 44, I think this is from the pre-trial brief and 102 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, are you saying the pre-trial brief was written by Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but these formulations in the pre-trial brief and in his report coincide. It doesn't matter who copied from whom and what came first, but I want to know what this witness established himself and what he took over as an established fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you ask the question, ask the Prosecution, not to Mr. Theunens. Or reformulate your question, whether he investigated and established those facts. And we have the -- we have heard his answer, that he based on documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I'm now asking whether Mr. Theunens still says that he established and that he knows what happened in Bijeljina on the 31st of March and the 1st and 2nd of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a fair question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, the last question is different from the earlier ones. But as I explained also in the methodology and in the scope of the report, I based myself on document -- on documents. And these documents are what I would call primary sources, i.e., documents established by those who participated in the operation or, for example, in the case of the JNA, if they did not participate who were in the area and who provided an account, as well as other official organs in the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, for example, there are a number of SJB reports discussing events during the take-over as well as the aftermath. And I used those documents in order to establish the -- or re-establish the events as I have described in my report. There is, of course, other material available like witness statements and so on, but for obvious reasons I have not used witness statements in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you then saying that Arkan and the local Serbs attacked Bijeljina on the 31st of March, took over power, killed 48 Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where that is written in my report, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, I found it. It's in the part dealing with the take-over of municipalities in Northern Bosnia. Is that tab 3 or 5 in your report? In fact, it's where the realisation of goals is discussed.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, we're referring to section 4 which in the English starts at page 109, but I don't remember writing anything about 44 Muslims -- or 48 Muslim civilians being killed, unless I quoted it from a primary source, but again I have no recollection of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here (e): "From the end of March to the 4th of April the Serb forces composed of Arkan's Tigers, a group of volunteers of SCP led by Mirko Blagojevic and other armed groups all operating under the supervision of -- under the control of the Bijeljina Crisis Staff took over power in Bijeljina. The take-over of power in Bijeljina corresponds to the first, second, and third strategic goals ...," and so on and so forth. And this is all completely in line with points 43 and 44 of the pre-trial brief and 102, probably, of the pre-trial brief. And then in your report, paragraph (f) deals with Zvornik -- paragraph 50 of your report. So you still say that what you wrote has been established?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes. Yes, Madam Uertz-Retzlaff --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- I was waiting for the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I'm not able to find what Mr. Karadzic is quoting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 110, subparagraph (e); and page 111, para (f), and he's referring to, I take it, pre-trial brief paras 44, 45, and 50.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, but it's not fair to quote from the pre-trial brief and mix it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's a separate question. Did you find the (e) and (f)?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 43, 44, and 102 in the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order for you to ask -- put questions in relation to the pre-trial brief, you have to ask first whether he's -- he had written that report -- pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I wrote -- which came first, the pre-trial brief or his report, because they are very similar. They are absolutely related. So I want to know who copied from whom. Did the OTP copy from the report or did he copy from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that can be answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can assure you, as I have attempted earlier, that I did not copy the pre-trial brief. Now, to answer Mr. Karadzic's specific question, I'm quoting now from the report, footnote 381 and 382 from the second part of the report. This is English pages 137, 138. The sentence, "During the night and the next day the Territorial Defence, the Serbian National Guard, and the Serbian Volunteer Guard started removing the barricades under the supervision of the Bijeljina Crisis Staff municipality ...," is taken from a Bijeljina SJB report which is mentioned in footnote 382. That is what I have tried to explain in the beginning. I don't invent facts. I didn't go on the ground. That is not part of my job. My job is to analyse and analyse documents, which means that any finding in the report -- I mean factual finding is based on documents and I have explained which documents I used. Any similarity between the pre-trial brief and my report, it's outside of my -- my powers. I did not participate in the drafting of the pre-trial brief. I don't know -- I do not know whether the Office of the Prosecutor used my report for the pre-trial brief or anything else. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you have page 110 and 111? The reason why you didn't put footnotes there is it is in the introductory part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's a summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So the summary is -- I started chapters or each section with a summary which contains findings of the rest -- of the -- of the actual section. And just to keep matters short, I didn't include footnotes there, but as I mentioned footnote 381 gives you the specific reference as to the role of the Crisis Staff, according to a Bosnian Serb Ministry of Interior organ in the take-over of Bijeljina and their relations or co-operation with the Serbian Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does this public security station report say that the Serbs took over power in Bijeljina and from whom?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document states that it took away -- I mean, that the Crisis Staff supervised the removal by the Bosnian Serb TO, the Serbian National Guard, and the Serbian Volunteer Guard of barricades that had been established by "Muslim extremists."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So to clarify this, before there was any action on the Serb side, someone put up barricades in Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we only considered that document, yes, that is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is there another document saying that before the crisis Arkan arrived in Bijeljina and that before the crisis anything was done in Bijeljina by Serb -- the Serb TO?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have such a document in my report, but, however, if Arkan is there, there is no information -- I mean, about how he arrived there. Now, from a military point of view he must have arrived before conducting this activity under the supervision of the Crisis Staff. If we're talking about the Bosnian Serb TO that is also participating in removing the barricades, it must have been established before. This is not the TO of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as it was envisaged in the -- in the doctrine of All People's Defence. I'm -- don't believe I have a document that explains when and how the Bosnian Serb TO was established in Bijeljina, but it's -- it's reasonable -- I mean, it's logical to conclude that it was established prior to removing these barricades.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know that this was the TO of the Bosnian Serbs, that the TO was not according to the administrative units? Who says this was the Territorial Defence of the Bosnian Serbs rather than the Territorial Defence of Bijeljina municipality?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I conclude this from looking at other documents that described the events during and after the take-over. Because we have a conflict between Serbs and Muslims or Bosniaks. I haven't seen any documents that would suggest or would indicate any co-operation between the regular TO of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Serbian Volunteer Guard or Serbian National Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I will now put something to you. This is how it was. Muslim extremists tried to throw a bomb on a Serb cafe. Shots were fired at them. Then they put up barricades all over town, took all the roof-tops, the top of the mosque, the spire of the church, and fired shots at Serb civilians. Then somebody called in Arkan, someone who did so unofficially. He arrived several hours after the crisis broke out. Then throughout this time the legal authorities of Bijeljina municipality were in session, whereas you say that it was the SDS Crisis Staff that was in session and overseeing all this. Is this how it was?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there are at least two different parts in your question. For the first part, I haven't seen any -- any evidence of that in the documents I consulted. If you now have a document that shows that, of course then I will take that in consideration. For the second part of your question, it is not me who states that the SDS Crisis Staff was in session and overseeing all this. I have referred to footnote 381 which is a document by the Bijeljina SJB. In addition, there is also a report - and that's footnote, excuse me, 384 - report by the SDS municipal board Bijeljina which is a report -- kind of situation report dated the 1st of April, 8.00 in the evening, which is sent to the SDS Main Board in Sarajevo, where the SDS Municipal Board informs the SDS Main Board about the events in Bijeljina. And there is no reference to the incidents you have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because that's not the first report, right, Mr. Theunens? Let us look at the document that you referred to now, 65 ter 1019. Let's have that in e-court. You said in your report that the Crisis Staff of the SDS of Bijeljina is informing the Main Staff about what they're doing; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Excuse me, it's informing the SDS Main Board, not the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Crisis Staff of the SDS of Bijeljina is informing the Main Board about what it is that the Crisis Staff is doing in Bijeljina; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- actually, it's informing -- as I said already in my answer, it's informing the SDS Main Board about the events in Bijeljina. And there is a reference to what they are doing. I mean, for example, it mentioned in the last paragraph: "We shall remain at the highest level of alert until further notice."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So in your view who was it that took over power in Bijeljina, or rather, which Crisis Staff was in charge of the take-over in Bijeljina, the SDS Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we -- can we not upload the document? I think it's the report cited in his report on page 138.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And it's Exhibit P2626; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This report of the Crisis Staff of Bijeljina 65 ter 1019, 1019 is the 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, P2626.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is quite illegible, but could we have the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we upload P -- Exhibit P2626.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, but it's the same document, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have the document. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on the basis of this document you are drawing the conclusion that the SDS of Bijeljina took over power in Bijeljina and is in charge of actions and informing the Main Staff about that; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this conclusion is not based on this specific document. It is based on a series of documents that can be found in that section. The first document I quoted is actually footnote 382, footnote 382 and 381. This is the SJB report that talks about the role of the Bijeljina Crisis Staff. Now, looking at the context - and I will give you more references - I concluded that this was the SDS Crisis Staff or the SDS-led Crisis Staff. First document for that is what we have now on the screen, which is footnote 384. I mean, the heading is clear, it says SDS Municipal Board Bijeljina Crisis Staff. And then I also quote JNA documents and there is footnote 389, which states that -- it's dated the 4th of April and it states: "The town of Bijeljina is controlled by the SDS and Arkan's men ...," and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us have a look at this or would you like us to look at this first or the police report? Where does it say that the Crisis Staff of the SDS took over power in Bijeljina? Can you help us so that we get to that document quickly?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the impression that Mr. Karadzic is trying to play -- is playing a game of words --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, let's -- we'll -- probably I take it that we'll see all the documents referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But what points can be taken from this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The one we have now on the screen, Your Honours, it shows to me, and again in the context of the other documents, that when -- the expression "Crisis Staff" when it's used at that time in the context of Bijeljina refers to the SDS-led crisis. And this report shows that the SDS-led Crisis Staff in Bijeljina informs the SDS Main Board of the situation in Bijeljina on the 1st of April at 2000. I mean, we can go into the details, but there is a discussion on what's happening, who spoke to whom, which statements were made. The authors also signed with Crisis Staff Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: All that can be taken from this document is that SDS Bijeljina Crisis Staff is reporting to its Main Board in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honours, and that's also what I put in footnote 383 in my report, part 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is a report of the Crisis Staff of the SDS of Bijeljina to the party about the behaviour of regular state organs; right? What is reported here is that recently the Council for National Defence of the Municipality of Bijeljina, which is a multi-ethnic body, a regular body of the municipality, held a meeting and adopted these conclusions where we can see these mixed patrols and everything else, all the other measures that were being taken by the regular authorities of the municipality of Bijeljina. And the Crisis Staff of the SDS is only providing information and they cannot do anything else but simply provide information about what the regular authorities of the municipality of Bijeljina are doing; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the first part of Mr. Karadzic's proposition, but when we look at the last sentence of this document, it states: "We shall remain at the highest level of alert until further notice ..." This goes beyond just reporting what is happening. The question could be raised as to why they have to remain at the highest level of alert and what that implies because if you're talking about the political party the question is: Why would they have to be at the highest level of alert and what does that mean in practice, and that's why I also include these other documents, the ones -- some of them I mentioned already. For example, situation reports by the JNA, 17th Corps which is the JNA unit in the area, that's, for example, footnote 388; as well as reports by the 2nd Military District, footnote 386. And there we see - and I have to add, I'm sorry, footnote 389 - that the role of the SDS in Bijeljina goes beyond simply providing information about what the regular authorities of the municipality of Bijeljina are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, are you trying to say that the SDS, apart from state organs, apart from their own representatives in state organs, did something else apart from providing information to its Main Board, its party Main Board? The Crisis Staff of the SDS, what are they doing here, are they describing what they did themselves or what the state organs did?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we are talking about footnote 384, they do both. They talk, indeed, about what state organs and political parties are doing, but they also talk about their own activities even if the latter is done in a very general manner. And that's why it's important to also look at other documentary evidence or reports discussing events that are taking place at the same time or at a similar time in the town of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, do help us then. Let us see whether the Crisis Staff of the party is issuing orders, instructions, is it acting in any other way but providing information to the Main Staff, or rather, the Main Board which is in accordance with what the Main Board told them to do. Do they -- do you have any documents that the party is doing anything except for what their representatives are doing in the legitimate organs of government?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, does --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness has actually now several times referred to a particular document that he has mentioned in his report and that he wants to rely on, and it is a 65 ter number. So perhaps it's advisable to look at it, and it would be 65 ter number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, but, Mr. Karadzic still remains on footnote 384, after which he will move on to the next document if he so wishes. But I think it's now time to conclude your question in relation to this document. Do you have any documents -- yes, it's time to move on to the next document. Have you exhausted your question in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want Mr. Theunens to tell me what is derived from this document. Was the SDS doing anything apart from the state organs. Did the board of the SDS do anything else but provide information and information about what the regular state organs were doing at that? The fact that they are going to remain alert is simply for the purpose of providing further information. Can you infer or conclude anything else on the basis of this document? And then let's be done with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: He answered that on page 94, from lines 18 to 24.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you then please help me with this report of the public security station. Let us see what it led you to conclude.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 65 ter number, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff? Do you have it, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no. I thought that I didn't need it, but -- but it has been mentioned by way of support for these allegations so I kindly ask that it be called up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would be 65 ter 09358, when that is footnote 381.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 380, 381, 382, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: All of these footnotes, then I just -- the first footnote --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think they are identical, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 381 and 382 are the same -- same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And I would just inform it's actually already a P number and P02629.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 01596 if I'm not mistaken. Am I right on that? 65 ter 01596? Can we please have the English version. It's going to be easier for us to find our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The chief of the public security station is reporting to the minister of the interior, and let us see what the date is. Can we establish what the date is?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- I put illegible for the date because I couldn't read it from the original B/C/S and in the translation it's not included. Now, from the events that are being described it has to be on or around -- I mean, after -- right after the 9th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have a report from the 2nd, 3rd, 4th April?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have such reports from the JNA, and they are included in footnotes 386, 387, 388, 3 -- excuse me, until 390. There is also -- I mean, sorry to continue with the answer. There is also an interesting document in footnote 393. When I say interesting, I mean relevant to establish the events in Bijeljina during and after the take-over, including the role of the Crisis Staff -- of the SDS Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Of the SDS or the municipality of Bijeljina? Let us be very specific, Mr. Theunens. The SDS or the municipality of Bijeljina? And do you distinguish between a party organ and a state organ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am talking about the SDS-led Crisis Staff in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, would you like to read this report in its entirety before being asked questions by the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I was answering another question. But yes, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's collapse the B/C/S and zoom -- I think it's a document of three pages. Please tell us -- let us know when you are done reading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Okay. Next page, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Can we have a look at the last paragraph where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let the witness read all the document and put your question afterwards.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Karadzic, but your question one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the last paragraph here does it say that the security situation in Bijeljina [In English] "... was disrupted on 31st of March, 1992, at about 8.30 probably hours in the evening when barricades were set up in the centre of the town by Muslim extremists."

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and that's also what I quoted in my report under footnote 382, as well as the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But did Serbs then start taking over government or did the Muslims start blockading town?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think these are two different issues, and this document talks -- I mean, when you look at the introduction of the document it talks about how the -- a person identified as Jesuric reports to the Ministry of the Interior of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on how he established an SJB, so a local public security station in Bijeljina. And he addresses some of the events that took place since he has received the instruction to establish a Bosnian Serb police station in Bijeljina. And of course -- I mean, from the context of the events it's logical to conclude that a Bosnian Serb police station can only be set up once the Bosnian Serbs have taken over control of the town from the regular authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who was in power in Bijeljina on the 31st of March or the 30th, 29th, 30th, 31st of March? What were the regular authorities if it was not the SDS that had won the elections?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's not a -- it may be there's an issue of translation or words, but it is not a party who -- I mean, it's not the SDS municipal board who is leading the town. It's the municipal council and the municipal authorities with the various bodies that are leading or that are in charge of the town. We -- we looked, for example, footnote 384 there was talk of -- it's called National Defence or the People's Defence Council in the municipality. These should not be party organs; these are state organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, these are not party organs. So who was in power on the 30th and 31st of March? Was that same entity, as it were, in power on the 5th of April as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I reviewed, the SDS takes over control of the town from somebody else. If you take over and somebody else has been -- if you take over control or take over power, then somebody else was in control or had the power before. I didn't analyse who was in power before, but it would be reasonable to conclude that those who were the regular municipal authorities, whereby I'm not familiar with their composition. But the documents I reviewed clearly state that it is the SDS that takes over control of the town of Bijeljina. And I refer to footnote 389 and 390, whereby this is the JNA stating that actually Bijeljina is controlled by the SDS and Arkan's men, indicating co-operation between the two, SDS and Arkan's men, Arkan's Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whose report is that? Whose document is that, 389, what you quoted just now?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's -- I mean, you find it on the bottom of English page 139. That is a report, a regular combat report, by the JNA 17th Corps to the 2nd -- JNA 2nd Military District dated the 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Theunens, do you know that the Serb Democratic Party won an absolute majority in 37 municipalities in Bosnia and a relative majority in ten more municipalities? So out of 109 municipalities, 47 municipalities had the SDS in power, and this power was shared by -- with the representatives of the Croats and Muslims. Do you know that in 47 municipalities the SDS was the party in power and that Bijeljina is included in those municipalities? So whoever it was that was in power on the 31st of March was in power on the 5th of April as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this proposition by Mr. Karadzic is not supported by the documents I reviewed and which I included in my report. These documents originating from different sources indicate that there is a take-over of power in Bijeljina by -- or led, excuse me, led by the SDS Crisis Staff in Bijeljina. And this take-over takes place on the 1st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Does this document in front of us talking about -- talk about take-over of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The document in front of us which was footnote 382 states that the Territorial Defence, whereby I conclude from the context looking also at the other documents that this is the Serb-established Bosnian Serb TO, together with the Serbian National Guard and the Serbian Volunteer Guard, they start to remove barricades which had been erected by what is called Muslim extremists under the supervision of the Bijeljina Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I refer or I mention footnotes in order to see or to have further information as to what happened in Bijeljina, I mean the footnotes 386 to -- until, actually, 393.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us finish with this document, Mr. Theunens. Does this document say that the SDS took over power or was a Crisis Staff established of the municipality of Bijeljina, SO Bijeljina? It went on for a brief period of time and then it grew into the War Presidency and the Crisis Staff of the SDS remained as an informative body. Do you have any proof of anything different?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
