utterances.text: Well, what I state -- because I'm not sure I entirely understand the question, that is, that the Crisis Staff we are talking about is the SDS Crisis Staff and they take over power -- I mean, they supervise the take-over of power, whereby they are assisted by Serbian Volunteer Guard and the Serbian National Guard and there are several documents, I mean the ones we have mentioned, that mention that. I have not discussed the War Presidency in detail there. It may well be that the Crisis Staff develops into a War Presidency, but I haven't analysed that. But at least on the 8th of April the SDS municipal board still issues instructions, footnote 395, to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, 395, is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at that document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have 65 ter number? Although it is cited in his report.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's definitely a 65 ter number. Ms. Elliott is just checking for it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 05872, under 395 it says 05872. Let's open it and see what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It should actually be a different number, but we will see. It should actually be the 65 ter number 08286.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the document, Your Honours. It is a handwritten document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have the document. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now I remember this document. Are you saying that this is an official document which reached the Presidency or is it a draft made by Mr. Kojic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document does not state that it is a draft. I mean, there is an addressee, there is a date, it is -- there is an author. Again, when looking at isolation, it may be difficult to understand what the document means, but this is why I -- I mean, this is why I would recommend to look at the documents in context --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Can we zoom in on the first line which seems to show the information as to the -- being faxed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, there is a line of a fax, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can collapse the English one for the moment. Yes. We show that whole page starting from fax. No, no, from the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have to see the top line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Top line. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not been able to establish who was the addressee of the document. But maybe also to better explain the overall, yeah, context, I would like to refer to footnote 109 in part 2, which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you, can you, read the date here on this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The date is at the bottom. Excuse me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, the top.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ah, the top for the fax. Yeah, well then we have to assume -- it says the 3rd of the 4th or the 4th of the 3rd, 1992, however in the bottom the document in handwritten says the 8th of April, so it may well be that the fax is not well programmed, I don't now. Because -- unless the -- the date, I mean the -- which states there as 8 should actually be a 3. That handwritten figure -- excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The handwritten note with the date should actually be the 3rd then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It's a 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's a 3 and then the 3rd in the fax addressee line also makes sense, so it should be the 3rd. But this correction in date does not -- for me does not change the conclusions I have included in my report as to relations between SDS and JNA and also the role of the SDS Municipal Board and the Crisis Staffs at the different levels in the structures the Serbs have established, like here the SAO Semberija and Majevica, their role in the take-over operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you say that this proves that the SDS Municipal Board issued instructions. You just said that. Is that right? Before we called up the document. Right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I mean, the author, the president of the SDS Main Board asked the organs of all Serbian Assemblies to support the decisions of the SAO Semberija Majevica Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Allow me, Mr. Theunens, to read this out slowly for the sake of all the participants and let the interpreters make sure I'm reading properly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's have both versions, English and B/C/S. Yes, continue, Mr. Karadzic, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what it says: "Municipal board SDS of BH Bijeljina."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the Crisis Staff mentioned here anywhere, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the part you have read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. "We ask the organs of all Serbian Assemblies to support the decisions of the SAO of Semberija and Majevica Crisis Staff and Serbian National Guard commanders. The entire Serbian people is organised into Territorial Defence units in the area of our district and the JNA is expected to refrain from conflict with the Serbian people. We are prepared to justify our firm positions by argument." Is this a request or an instruction, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be both. If you ask somebody to do that and you are in a position of authority, then it becomes an instruction. Now, in my report I have identified it as a request because I didn't have the opportunity to delve into this particular document further as to see whether the author was, indeed, in a position to issue instructions to the addressees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Theunens, to which Serbian Assembly this is addressed? How can the Municipal Board be an authority for the Assemblies of which it is asking something?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the document again, it -- I would have to check again in the exact position of Mr. Savo Kojic, because, okay, he signs as the president of the SDS -- SDS Main Board, and instead of SDS Municipal Board Bijeljina being the originator of the document, as I put in my report, this research on Savo Kojic would allow you to establish whether it is sent by the SDS Bijeljina Municipal Board or sent to the SDS Municipal Board and that would of course allow to answer your question. But even if we would make that correction, if needed, of the report, again it wouldn't change the conclusions I have drawn on role of the SDS in the take-over, Bijeljina or other municipalities, nor on the relations SDS-dominated Bosnian Serb structures develop with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you keep saying that, but from whom would the SDS be taking over power when it is already in power, from whom?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that I have answered that question. There is a difference between regular municipal authorities being in power and, on the other hand, party organs or party-dominated bodies being in power. And again, that is also explained in the documents I have discussed. I mean, I can -- if you want I can list you another one, footnote 393, there the 17th Corps informs the 2nd Military District that the Bijeljina Crisis Staff does not allow mobilisation of one of its units. Now, if this was a regular state body, as it was envisaged before the outbreak of hostilities or before the take-overs, better, I mean measures would be taken because there were clear rules and regulations as to roles of municipal authorities in the system of All People's Defence. But now we're talking about other bodies, we're talking about SDS-dominated Crisis Staffs on the level of municipalities, we're talking about SAOs. These are all new structures that the SDS has established and they don't respond to the regular authorities of the -- of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They don't involve representatives of other political parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who says that, Mr. Theunens? How did you conclude that anything changed in the municipal government on that date?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you allow me, I would like to refer to footnote 109, where Mr. Karadzic speaks during the 14th Session of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is discussed on page 31 of part 2 of the report, English version. Mr. Karadzic there calls upon the delegates to establish Crisis Staffs in their municipalities, in particular in the newly founded ones. And he also urges the delegates to try to organise the people so that they can defend themselves, and so on. I just skip one sentence now in order not to spend too much time. They should organise Territorial Defence and if the JNA's there they must be placed under its command. Now, to me -- and again, looking at all the other documents I reviewed, I mean footnote 107 are instructions -- excuse me, 106, instructions for the organisation and activity of organs of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a state of emergency. These and other documents I have included in my report indicate that we are -- I mean, that SDS is organising and establishing, creating, political -- or governing bodies on different levels, on the municipality level. They establish SAOs. There were no SAOs in Bosnia-Herzegovina before the SDS-led Bosnian Serbs decided to establish those or the ARK -- I mean Serb autonomous districts as well as the Autonomous Region of Krajina. These were not regular structures in Bosnia-Herzegovina prior to the establishment is it in the end of 1991 or early 1992. And this is why I conclude also then when we talk about these bodies, as I just mentioned, they were newly established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let's finish with this document first. It doesn't say president here, it says forward to the Main Board. So the president of the SDS Main Board, this is a mistranslation. So it's actually not the president of the SDS Main Board but the president of the Municipal Board. That's one thing. And secondly, he's expecting the JNA not to interfere, which would indicate that he was afraid of the JNA, not that he was in complicity with the JNA. So he wants the JNA to refrain from getting involved in the conflict.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are obviously right about the position of Savo Kojic and I apologise for the misunderstanding that I created but it was an issue of editing, that text, "president of the SDS Main Board," actually moved in my report. For the second part of your question, that is your interpretation. We have discussed this morning in examination the report dated the 20th of March by General Kukanjac, commander of the 2nd Military District where he talks about overall the -- I would say consistency between the objectives of the SDS and the SDA, at that moment in time, even if they are, according to him, some examples in the SDS of people, for example, who distrust the JNA or consider the JNA as Communists. But I think, yes, by the date of this document, 3rd of April, we do see in many parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina with the Serbian or significant Serbian presence, that there is co-operation or at least good relations between the JNA and the SDS. And I would refer to the specific documents including documents on take-overs to substantiate that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by Serbian presence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, there was -- in Bosnia-Herzegovina there were people of different ethnicities. There were a number -- there were a number of officially recognised nationalities in the SFRY, and Bosnia-Herzegovina was an example of a republic where different ethnic groups or nationalities were living. And in addition to the nationalities there were also minorities -- or there was at least one minority. I mean, there were -- Serb was an official nationality, Croatian, Muslim, people like -- there were people who could -- who identified themselves as Yugoslavs, there were Macedonians, there were Slovenes, Albanians were a minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. When you say "Serb presence," do you mean by that that at that point in time there were about 32 per cent of Serbs there and that they were in the majority occupying over -- or rather being present on over 60 per cent of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina where they had always lived, and that they took over power in 67 municipalities. So is it quite natural that their presence there should be what it was?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not analysed that in my report. I mean, this is a very political issue and I know when I was working for UNPROFOR, for example, that in the calculations or the percentages of territory that were referred to in the various peace plans that were proposed by the international community throughout the conflict, the amounts of territory was always an issue and the Bosnian Serbs always claimed or stated that their number, be it 32 per cent or 33, was not an accurate reflection of the percentage of territory they controlled, i.e., they always stated that they controlled a larger territory because they lived outside of cities and so on, and so on, but that is not something that I have analysed in the context of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we finish with this document. Is it correct that here a president of the Municipal Board is asking the Main Board to intervene with the Assembly to support their decisions to keep the JNA at arm's length for them; right or not right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is not my understanding of the report -- of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document means? Do you abide by the conclusion you reached in your report on the basis of this document that the SDS Main Board was issuing instructions; that it became the authority, the government in Bijeljina; that the Serbs in Bijeljina took over power from someone; that they were in collusion with the JNA, whereas this document shows exactly the opposite?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's exactly part of the methodology, that is, that an analyst does not draw a conclusion on the basis of one single report unless it's a conclusion confined to that one single report or document. The conclusions I have drawn on my analysis on the events in Bijeljina say between 31st of March and 15th of April are based on a series of documents and that is what I have attempted to reflect in my report. In relation to this specific document, footnote 395, my conclusion is only that -- I mean, is a reflection of the document, that is, that according to the Bijeljina SDS Municipal Board, the entire Serbian people is organising TO units and the JNA is expected to refrain from conflict with the Serbian people. And when we then look at other documents we have -- I have included, then we see that actually there is a consistency between the views of the -- and expectations of the Bijeljina SDS Municipal Board and the JNA 2nd Military District for what relations between the Serbian people or the SDS and the JNA is concerned at that moment in time. And I mean JNA 2nd Military District, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To conclude with this document, did you cite it as a document corroborating your thesis, that the Serbs in Bijeljina took over power; and if so, can you tell us from whom?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just answered the questions, Your Honour. I did include it in the section "Bijeljina," but I do not use this document to conclude that as -- excuse me, I don't use this document as the sole or the only basis for my conclusion that the Serbs, Bosnian Serbs, by the SDS, have taken over power in Bijeljina. I have used other documents for that and I have read out the footnote several times already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at the document which led you to establish that the Serbs took over power in Bijeljina from someone?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, we will admit this document, but that interpretation has been revised -- has to be revised, in particular in relation to the last line. We'll give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1585, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: And the date, Mr. President, should also be revised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can we now look at the document which led you to this conclusion, that the Serbs started and I'll tell you what you said. You said, probably judging by analogy, that if such large-scale take-overs of power were being conducted by the Serbs, this had to be planned, well-co-ordinated, and it had to count on the surprise factor. Did you say that on your general part on the take-over of power, planned, co-ordinated, and counting on the surprise factor? How did the Serbs manage to surprise themselves with Muslim barricades and Muslim snipers in the centre of Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's homework for Mr. Theunens for tonight. We'll rise today and resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. And I take it you understand it that you're not supposed to talk with anybody else about your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.58 p.m.,
